content: I'm planning to open some issues -- one issue per statement -- on the repo to explicitely flag various sorrys for which (i) the statement isn't expected to change anytime soon, (ii) we want proofs, (iii) none of the core contributors are likely to spend time on proving these. If there's anything you would like to flag please let me know (or feel free to just open an issue yourself).
I think the repo needs a bit more clean-up for more of these statements to be available. For now the coding theory stuff is probably the best bet

Yeah coding theory has a few which should be stable I think -- or stable to the extent that any proof repair due to a small definition change (e.g. some type R becomes R>=0 or w/e) would be easy to repair. SOme of polynomial stuff should also be ok I think? Then there's the Merkle tree stuff but some of these are todos rather than sorrys...

I'm also ok with some proofs breaking if it comes to it -- some proofs will break every now and then anyway -- I just don't want to include anything that is definitely getting replaced in the foreseeable future.
And it's also be able to keep track of existing sorrys better than I currently do (seeing warnings when building/running some script that returns sorrys/...)

Alexander Hicks said:

Then there's the Merkle tree stuff but some of these are todos rather than sorrys...

I have just done some reorganizing. The sorries in the InductiveMerkleTree folder are things I did not turn out to need for the completeness proof, so I don't expect to spend time proving these soon, but they could be useful down the line, so I'd still like proofs.

The sorries in Oracle.lean are needed for the completeness proof, so my desire for proofs there is greater, but they are really VCVio lemmas, so I'm nervous they'll change.

As an update: many of these have now been filled in by Logical Intelligence's AI tool (pending review of the PRs, aiming to do so tomorrow). :slight_smile:
Hoping this indicates a path to removing all sorrys from Data/, ToMathLib/, and so on quite soon.
Not necessarily related to the project per se, but perhaps the Logical Intelligence folks would be interested in this #announce > SorryDB Hackathon

Hello! I'm mathematician looking to get into crypto and FV, I was recently introduced to this project by a friend, I'm new to FV and crypto but I'm excited to do some work in these areas and learn. I am happy to help fill in some of these missing proofs, I just submitted a small PR the other day. I am happy to just keep looking through the issues labelled "proof wanted" but if there are other areas that would be more helpful for me to plug into I am certainly up to hear about them.

Sounds great! Most core ArkLib contributors were in Cambridge last week but as we all get back to work I'll look to open some more issues in ArkLib (and review your PR!). There are also issues you might find interesting in https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean and (soon) https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/VCV-io.
Thanks! I'll take a look at those.
